question: How long can I take to cool cooked rice?
answer: Cooked rice must be cooled from 135 °F to 70 °F within 2 hours, and then from 70 °F to 41 °F within an additional 4 hours — a total of 6 hours.

citations.doc: FDA Food Code §3-501 — Holding and Cooling
citations.heading: Cooling cooked food
citations.snippet: Cooked TCS food, including cooked rice, must be cooled from 135°F to 70°F (57°C to 21°C) within 2 hours, and from 70°F to 41°F (21°C to 5°C) within an additional 4 hours — 6 hours total.

passages.doc: FDA Food Code §3-501 — Holding and Cooling
passages.heading: Cooling cooked food
passages.text:
Cooling cooked food
TCS foods held hot must be maintained at 135°F (57°C) or above. Food that
falls below 135°F for more than 4 hours must be discarded.
Cooked TCS food, including cooked rice, must be cooled from 135°F to 70°F
(57°C to 21°C) within 2 hours, and from 70°F to 41°F (21°C to 5°C) within an
additional 4 hours — 6 hours total. Use shallow pans, ice baths, or ice
paddles to speed cooling.

Ready-to-eat TCS food held longer than 24 hours must be date-marked and

passages.doc: FDA Food Code §3-501 — Holding and Cooling
passages.heading: Hot holding
passages.text:
Hot holding
TCS foods held cold must be maintained at 41°F (5°C) or below. Examples
include cut leafy greens, cut tomatoes, cut melons, cooked rice, dairy, and
raw or cooked meats held for later service.
TCS foods held hot must be maintained at 135°F (57°C) or above. Food that
falls below 135°F for more than 4 hours must be discarded.

passages.doc: FDA Food Code §3-501 — Holding and Cooling
passages.heading: Cold holding
passages.text:
Cold holding
TCS foods held cold must be maintained at 41°F (5°C) or below. Examples
include cut leafy greens, cut tomatoes, cut melons, cooked rice, dairy, and
raw or cooked meats held for later service.
